name: Quigley Cripple
imitates: A crippled mayfly dun stuck in its shuck, with a marabou tail-and-abdomen and a deer hair wing; Bob Quigley's design works for most mayfly hatches when sizes and colors are changed.

steps.text: Start the thread, tie in a piece of fine copper wire and wrap back over it to the bend.
Peel several marabou fibers off a feather, even their tips and tie them in at the bend with two turns. The tail should be about half a shank long.
Lift the marabou butt ends out of the way and bring the thread forward to the starting point.
Wrap the marabou butts forward to the starting point as the abdomen and tie off. Clip the excess.
Spiral the copper wire forward through the marabou abdomen, tie it off at the front and clip the excess.
Dub a small ball of superfine dubbing at the front of the abdomen, leaving at least an eye length of bare shank ahead of it.
Cut, clean and stack a clump of deer hair, measured to a shank length.
Tie the deer hair in just ahead of the dubbing with several tight turns and clip the butts to a short brush.
Tie in a grizzly hackle by its butt in the space between the hair butts and the base of the hair tips.
Wrap the hackle three turns, tie off and clip. Whip finish and trim the thread.
